attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the demand context, the 'little evidence' core and the 'I'd argue' causal clause. The statement has a causal structure, but only the descriptive core can be checked.

contract.note: Reading 'user adoption' as workplace genAI use generally is an ordinary reading, given the section is about AI's prevalence. The speaker may have meant enterprise-bought features only, and no data isolates those. Leaving the hedged causal clause ungraded is fair.

evidence.note: Official Census BTOS data published before the post: under 8% of even the largest firms used AI by Aug 2024. This backs the firm-level part of the descriptive core.
NBER summary of a nationally representative Aug 2024 survey, public before the post: 28% of workers used genAI for their job. That is evidence of significant worker-level use.

reviews.rationale: Only the descriptive core is scored. Firm-level official data (e1) fit 'little evidence of significant adoption'. A representative worker survey available before the post (e2) shows over a quarter of workers using genAI at work, against the claim. Both of the contract's conditions are partly met, so the result is mixed. The hedged causal argument is not tested.

attribution.note: Zitron's own judgment. The 500M target is attributed to Pichai, but the 'unrealistic' verdict is Zitron's.

semantics.note: 'So unrealistic' that the CEO should be fired is a categorical judgment that the target won't be met, not a graded probability. The firing remark is normative and is correctly left unscored.

contract.note: Using Google's reported Gemini app MAU is the ordinary measure of Pichai's 'used by' target. Reading 'unrealistic' as a firm expectation of a miss fits the strength of his wording.

evidence.note: Official Q3 2025 CEO remarks (2025-10-29): Gemini app had over 650M MAU, before the deadline. This is a company disclosure, but it is the source the contract specifies.
750M MAU reported Feb 2026, after the deadline. It shows the trend continuing but does not decide the outcome.
News report of a court-disclosed 350M MAU in March 2025. It shows the growth path but not that the target was reached.

reviews.rationale: Zitron called 500M Gemini users by end-2025 so unrealistic as to be a firing offence. Google officially reported over 650M monthly Gemini app users on 2025-10-29, before the deadline. The deadline has passed and the target was exceeded. The MAU definition is not independently audited, but it is the measure Google uses for this goal.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful: keeps 'categorically failed', the hedged 'appears' and 'similarly-useless'. 'Similarly-useless' is opinion.

contract.note: The contract reads 'failed to productize' as having little or no paid API or subscription business. In the same passage Zitron cites Anthropic's revenue, its API share and its Claude consumer app, so he plainly meant no meaningful or differentiated products. The contract's reading makes him contradict himself, which stretches it against him.

evidence.note: S-1 filed 2026-10-26, before the evaluation date: Claude launched commercially in Q1 2023. This would contradict only the literal reading the contract uses.
S-1: 2024 revenue of $386M, with consumption and subscription revenue both growing. It shows sales, which the speaker himself acknowledged. It does not test his sense of 'productize'.
Anthropic's Sept 2024 Claude Enterprise launch. It bears on the hedged 'only product appears' aside, which is not scored separately.
Anthropic called Computer Use experimental and error-prone. This matches the subsidiary remark, which the contract says does not decide the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The contract's plain reading, that Anthropic had no paid products, is not the speaker's meaning. He acknowledges Anthropic's revenue and API business in the same passage. His actual claim is that it failed to build meaningful products beyond the model, and that has no measurable threshold. Scoring it as contradicted by revenue figures would be unfair, so it is not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps his 'I do not believe' framing, his own definition of a 'real' industry and the subsidy reason.

contract.note: Treating the claim as not adjudicable is fair. It is a label under a personal definition with no thresholds, and 'entirely subsidized' is hyperbole with no stated measure.

reviews.rationale: Whether generative AI is a 'real' industry under Zitron's own definition depends on undefined terms: sustainable revenue, meaningful products, actual market penetration. 'Entirely subsidized' has no stated threshold. No evidence was attached, and none could settle a label like this. Not adjudicable.
